+MailerLite cut its Free plan to 250 active subscribers and 2,500 emails per month, down from 500 subscribers and 12,000 emails, and capped free accounts at 3 automations, 3 forms, and 1 landing page. +MailerLite reduced its Free plan effective June 16, 2026, with existing free accounts moving to the new limits on July 1. The free tier drops to 250 active subscribers and 2,500 emails per month, down from 500 subscribers and 12,000 emails. It also caps free accounts at 3 active automations, 3 forms, 1 landing page, and 1 website. Existing free accounts transitioned automatically, and if your list is over 250 contacts, you cannot send campaigns until you upgrade or reduce your subscriber count.

+If you build on a free plan, this is a real change worth a few minutes of attention. The good news: your data is not deleted, you have time to plan, and you have options. This guide breaks down exactly what is changing, how to tell if you are affected, and the three sensible paths forward, including the most generous free alternatives if you would rather not pay yet.
+Already shopping around? See our full roundup of MailerLite alternatives for the complete side-by-side picture.

+Quick context: Mailsoftly’s free plan gives you 500 contacts (double the new MailerLite limit) and 2,000 emails a month sent from your Gmail, Outlook, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account, plus automation, segmentation, and real human support, with no credit card.
+Since July 1, 2026, MailerLite’s Free plan is capped at 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails per month, with caps of 3 automations, 3 forms, and 1 landing page.
+If you are over 250 subscribers, sending campaigns, running automations, and manually adding contacts stop working until you upgrade or trim your list. Your data stays intact.
+You get two free seats and some new features (HTML editor, more templates, pop-ups), so the change is a trade, not a pure cut.
+Three options: trim your list to stay free, upgrade to a paid plan (MailerLite starts at $12 per month), or switch to a more generous free plan such as Mailsoftly (500 contacts) or Kit.
+What is changing on the MailerLite Free plan?

+On July 1, 2026, MailerLite’s Free plan moved to lower usage limits while unlocking a handful of features that used to be paid-only. The headline numbers are the subscriber cap and the monthly send limit, both of which drop sharply. Feature-use limits on automations, forms, and pages follow shortly after, with enforcement planned for August. Here is the before and after.

+Source: the official MailerLite Free plan update documentation. Newly introduced caps on automations, forms, and pages are planned for enforcement in August 2026. Campaigns themselves remain unlimited within the monthly send cap.

+It is not all reductions. Free accounts gain a second user seat and pick up features that were previously locked to paid plans, including a custom HTML campaign editor, more campaign and landing page templates, blogs, and promotional pop-ups, which the official MailerLite features overview lists in full. So the change is best understood as a trade: richer tooling for a much smaller usage allowance. For a frame of reference on how MailerLite priced before this, our MailerLite pricing breakdown walks through the paid tiers.
+Want headroom without paying yet? Mailsoftly’s free plan gives 500 contacts and keeps your automations on as you grow.Start free with Mailsoftly →
+Am I affected by the new limits?

+You are affected if your MailerLite account is on the Free plan and exceeds any of the new limits. The most common trigger is the subscriber count: many free users sit between 250 and 500 contacts today, which was fine under the old cap but is over the new one. Run through this quick checklist now.
+Are you over the new free limits?
+✓More than 250 active subscribers on your list
+✓Sending more than 2,500 emails a month (subscribers multiplied by campaigns)
+✓Running more than 3 active automations or relying on more than 3 forms
+✓Using more than one landing page or website builder site

+If you ticked any box, plan ahead so a launch or a scheduled send does not get blocked. If none apply, you are fine, and you actually gain a second seat and the new features. Not sure how much room you have? It helps to understand how providers count contacts and sends in the first place, which our primer on email marketing fundamentals covers alongside list hygiene and deliverability.
+What happens if you go over the limit?

+If you are over 250 subscribers, MailerLite pauses your ability to send campaigns, run automations, and manually add new subscribers until you either upgrade to a paid plan that fits your list or reduce your subscriber count below 250. If you stay within the subscriber cap but exceed the 2,500 monthly email limit, campaign and automation sends stop for the rest of that month. Importantly, your account and data are not deleted, so nothing is lost while you decide.

+The 12,000 to 2,500 email cut is the one that surprises people. A 250-contact list emailed twice a week already uses about 2,000 sends a month, so even a small, engaged list can hit the ceiling fast. If sending pauses mid-month, your newsletter or automated welcome series simply stops going out until the next cycle or an upgrade.

+There is no single right answer; it depends on your list size, how often you send, and whether you are ready to pay. Broadly, you have three sensible paths: trim your list to stay free, upgrade MailerLite, or switch to a more generous free plan.

An AI notetaker records the call and writes the notes. An AI meeting assistant also does the work that follows: it updates your CRM, drafts the follow-up, briefs you before the next call and answers questions across all your meetings. tl;dv does both.
Which meeting platforms does the tl;dv notetaker work with?
